Intestinal bacterial colonization produces toxin-mediated neuromuscular-junction paralysis; respiratory weakness and diplopia do not establish lung or eye damage.
RPE65-related rod-cone retinal degeneration with progressive visual impairment.

HSV-1 infection of genital skin and mucocutaneous surfaces, characteristically producing vesicles and ulcers.
Inherited retinal dystrophy; retinal degeneration defines the affected organ.
Benign smooth-muscle tumor arising in the liver; the definition does not support the endocrine parent classification.
Sulfatide storage causes central and peripheral demyelination; optic atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Weakness is neurogenic; cholecystitis is <30%.
Clonal myeloproliferation with marrow fibrosis; hepatic extramedullary hematopoietic infiltration occurs in roughly 40-70%. Splenic involvement shares the blood axis.
Squamous carcinoma originates in the nasal cavity or paranasal sinuses, included in the pulmonary axis.
Benign tumor of the tongue; oral structures belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Defined by limb syndactyly/polydactyly and sternal malformations; intellectual disability occurs in only 5-29%.
Adenocarcinoma originates in and infiltrates the stomach; no additional organ consistently meets the involvement threshold.
Germ-cell tumor arising in the CNS; endocrine dysfunction depends on tumor location and is not established above 30% across the group.
Defined by intellectual disability and skeletal overgrowth/dysplasia; scoliosis occurs in 4/13. Cardiac defects are generally <30%; obesity is a separate condition.
